newRun.title: New inventory run
newRun.hint: Pick a paging scheme and parameters. The run uses the currently initialized scene.
newRun.useGroupingHint: Periodic paging only. Devices are split into $N_g$ groups; each paging round invites one group in turn. A device joins the group of the first paging it hears (first-catch) and stays aligned to that group's paging times. Off: every paging round invites all devices.
newRun.useCaptureHint: When several devices pick the same Msg1 slot, the reader still decodes the strongest one if it is at least 6 dB above the next strongest. Off: every slot with two or more devices is a collision. For periodic paging the Msg2/Msg3 allocation is $0.5\,K$ with capture and $0.37\,K$ without.
newRun.useEbiHint: EBI is the early indicator (EI) of the aperiodic paper: after Msg1 the reader sends a one-bit flag per slot saying whether a response was detected, so devices know where their Msg2 is. On: each round spends that extra EI air time, and the reader's energy detector is modelled with false alarms and missed detections. Off: no EI time and ideal slot detection.
newRun.includeD2rHint: D2R is the device-to-reader uplink. On: a reader covers a device only if both legs close, so the range is $\min(R2D, D2R)$, as in the paper. Off: only the reader-to-device leg (power-up and paging) counts, which overstates coverage.
newRun.disableReadersHint: Checked readers are skipped for this run (handy for single-reader baselines).
newRun.allReadersDisabledWarning: All readers disabled — no device will be identified.
newRun.endHint: The run ends when every reachable device is identified, when nothing new is identified for the time above, or when you pause / stop it. Devices outside every reader’s coverage are marked unreachable at start; devices never identified are shown as red dots.

charts.timeBin: Simulated time (s, all readers per bin)

ident.lead: Devices identified so far versus simulated time.
ident.body: X axis is simulated time, Y axis is how many devices some reader has successfully inventoried by then (count or percent). With one reader selected, only devices inside its coverage count. The earlier the curve reaches the top, the faster the inventory. T50 / T90 / T99 are read off this curve. The vertical line is the current live or replay time.

controller.lead: Per round: frame size K, access probability p*, and backlog estimate n̂.
controller.body: Top: K is the number of M1 slots the reader opens in this round (frame length), p* is the probability a device takes part; both are adjusted by the estimator from the previous round. Bottom: n̂ is how many devices the estimator believes are still unidentified, 'true backlog' is the real number, 'joiners' is how many actually took part. n̂ close to the true backlog means the estimator is accurate. With all readers selected only K and the true backlog are drawn, one line per reader.

outcome.lead: How each M1 slot ended, and the share of useful slots.
outcome.body: Each bar is one round (a time bin when all readers are shown), stacked by outcome: success = exactly one device answered, collision = several answered at once and drowned each other, empty = nobody answered. Resource efficiency = success / all slots, on the right axis in percent. Pure slotted ALOHA tops out around 36.8%.

timing.lead: How long each stage of a round took, in milliseconds.
timing.body: A round is paging (reader broadcasts the page) → M1 (devices answer in one of K random slots) → EBI (the reader broadcasts a K-bit map of which M1 slots it decoded) → M2 (reader acknowledges each winner) → M3 (device confirms). The stacked height is the whole round. Larger K makes M1 longer; more successes make M2 / M3 longer. With all readers selected the bars are averages per round within each time bin.

energy.lead: Stored energy of the devices now, and protocol energy spent over time.
energy.body: Left: histogram of the energy (µJ) each in-scope device has in its capacitor at the current time; devices on the far left are about to switch off. Right: cumulative energy each device type has spent sending and receiving protocol messages. A device that runs out mid-round is forced off to recharge and competes again later; those events are counted as depletions in Metrics.

round.lead: Slot-by-slot view of one M1 frame.
round.body: Each cell is one M1 slot: idle, single (one device, decoded), captured (several devices, the strongest was decoded), collision, or missed. The numbers above: candidates = awake devices allowed to take part; joiners = those that actually did, after p*; budget = how many winners M2 can acknowledge this round; budget dropped = winners not acknowledged for lack of budget, who retry next round; identified = devices finished in this round; true backlog = devices in this reader's coverage still unidentified. Use the slider to pick a round or follow the latest one.

metrics.lead: Summary numbers and breakdown tables for this run.
metrics.body: Cards: identified / unidentified / resource efficiency / rounds / depletions / unreachable. Per type: count, identified, T50, T99 and energy per device type. Depletions by stage: in which stage devices ran out of energy. Time overhead: total time and share per stage. Per reader: rounds, identified and efficiency for each reader.

pin.lead: Distribution of the strongest power each device receives from any reader.
pin.body: X axis is received power (dBm), Y axis is the fraction of devices receiving at most that power. A curve further right means devices are closer to a reader and harvest faster. One line per device type; compare with Figure 4 of the paper.

terms.identified: Devices a reader has successfully inventoried.
terms.dropped: Devices still unidentified when the run ended: outside every reader’s coverage, time limit reached, or no progress (shown as red dots).
terms.unreachable: Devices outside every reader's coverage; they can never be inventoried.
terms.no_progress: The run ended by itself after the configured stall time (default 300 s simulated) without a single new identification.
terms.depletions: Times a device ran out of energy in the middle of a round and had to recharge.
terms.rounds: Rounds executed so far, all readers together.
terms.t50: T50 / T90 / T99: simulated time until 50 / 90 / 99 % of the devices were identified.
terms.K: Frame size: number of M1 slots in this round.
terms.pstar: p*: probability that an awake device takes part in this round.
terms.nHat: n̂: the estimator's guess of how many devices are still unidentified.
terms.backlogTrue: True backlog: actual number of unidentified devices in coverage.
terms.joiners: Devices that actually took part in the round after the p* draw.
terms.candidates: Awake devices that were allowed to take part.
terms.success: Slot with exactly one answering device.
terms.collision: Slot where several devices answered at once; none decoded.
terms.efficiency: Resource efficiency: successful slots divided by all slots.
terms.paging: Paging: the reader broadcasts the round parameters.
terms.m1: M1: devices answer in one of K random slots.
terms.ebi: EBI: the reader broadcasts a K-bit map of which M1 slots it decoded; its length grows with K.
terms.m2: M2: the reader acknowledges each decoded device.
terms.m3: M3: the acknowledged device replies and is identified.
terms.budget: Maximum number of winners M2 can acknowledge this round.
terms.budgetDropped: Winners not acknowledged because the budget ran out; they retry next round.
terms.energyNow: Energy stored in the device capacitor at the current time.
terms.energySpent: Cumulative energy spent on protocol messages.
terms.slotCodes: Cell colours: idle, single, captured, collision, missed.
terms.pin: Pin: strongest received power from any reader, in dBm.
terms.cdf: CDF: fraction of devices at or below the value on the X axis.
